status: frozen before the depth experiments; the main line of the study
question: Which image operations are programmable in the weight space of a SIREN without training, by which layer, with what error, and how does programmability degrade with depth? Where it fails, what weight-only quantity predicts the failure?
framing: A SIREN f(p) = A_L sin(... sin(A1 p + c1) ...) + c_L separates into a coordinate layer (A1, c1), a dictionary (the hidden sine layers) and a linear readout (A_L, c_L). Coordinate-domain operations act on layer 1 exactly; pointwise value maps act on the readout exactly; spectrum-changing operations (filtering, morphology) must re-weight the dictionary. For one sine layer the dictionary is a set of plane waves and an isotropic Gaussian blur is exactly a per-unit attenuation of the readout, A2_i *= exp(-|w_i|^2 sigma^2 / 2). Each further sine layer turns plane waves into harmonic mixtures (frequencies sum_i n_i w_i), and no per-unit attenuation is exact.

zoos.networks: test_00000..test_00019 of each; MNIST test images, 2,000 Adam steps

programs.rms_attenuation: weight-only generalisation to any depth: attenuate the readout row of hidden unit j of the last sine layer by exp(-nu_j^2 sigma^2 / 2), where nu_j^2 is the mean-square spatial frequency of that unit's pre-activation gradient, computed from the weights alone (for L=3: nu_j^2 = 1/2 sum_i A2_ij^2 |w_i|^2; for deeper nets recursively with the same half-power rule). Exact when each unit carries one harmonic; a heuristic otherwise.
programs.frozen_dictionary_bound: least squares of the readout on the target image: the best any readout-only program can do (uses the target, so an upper bound on programmability of the readout, not a weight-only program)
programs.finetune: Adam 10 / 50 / 200 steps from the original network: what training does with the same or more function evaluations

weight_only_failure_predictor: harmonic index H_j of a hidden unit of the last sine layer = the total phase swing of its pre-activation beyond the first harmonic, estimated from the weights as sum_i |A2_ij| (the amplitude of the argument of the sine; when it is below about 1 the unit is nearly a single harmonic, when it is several radians the unit is a strongly harmonic mixture). The network-level index is the readout-weighted mean of H_j.

predictions_frozen_before_running.Q1_exactness: On L2w64 and L2w32, exact_shallow_blur reaches MSE below 2e-4 on every network for sigma = 1 pixel (the only error is the discrete sampling of the target).
predictions_frozen_before_running.Q2_depth_degrades: On L3w32 and L4w32, rms_attenuation stays above the frozen_dictionary_bound on at least 18 of 20 networks each, and its median MSE ratio to no_edit is between 0.3 and 0.9 (a partial blur, never a clean one).
predictions_frozen_before_running.Q3_failure_is_predicted_by_harmonics: Across the 40 deep networks, the per-network MSE of rms_attenuation (relative to no_edit) correlates positively with the network-level harmonic index (Spearman rho > 0.4).
predictions_frozen_before_running.Q4_readout_only_cannot_do_morphology: On L3w32, the frozen_dictionary_bound for dilate and erode is above 0.5 x no_edit MSE on at least 15 of 20 networks: these operations need hidden-layer changes, whereas for blur_1 the bound is below 0.5 x no_edit on at least 15 of 20.
predictions_frozen_before_running.Q5_learned_editors_lose_to_algebra: contrast_2 by the readout affine map gives MSE below 1e-6 on every network of every zoo, against the published learned-editor results of about 0.02 on the NFN/NFT CIFAR contrast task (different zoo, same operation; reported as a qualitative comparison, not a controlled one, until the NFN zoo is reproduced).

controls: every number on 20 networks per zoo with image-bootstrap 95% intervals
masks where the target is undefined
targets derived from the network's own rendering, not the MNIST image, so fitting error does not enter
the shallow zoos fit poorly (about 24 dB); conclusions about exactness concern the function the network represents, not image quality
decision_rule: If Q1-Q3 hold, the depth result and the failure predictor become the paper's centre, and the next node extends to high-pass / band-pass filters and to multi-sigma blur. If Q3 fails (no correlation), the failure theory is wrong and the next node tests the harmonic expansion directly with per-unit spectra from a single forward pass of each unit (allowed here: this is analysis, not the capability protocol).
